# Decision memo: Prioritize billing policy clarity and free-tier expectations

*Generated by `gpt-6-luna` from saved aggregates (2026-10-06T18:57:50-0700); every number cites a claim ID in `claims.csv` / `claims_extra.csv`. Code check: passed.*

## Recommendation
Prioritize billing/support, starting with `billing.premium_paywall`. This is primarily a deliberate product/pricing policy issue—not a broken feature—so effort should clarify restrictions and premium requirements, and assess whether free-tier limits are communicated and experienced as intended. Do not treat generic dissatisfaction, `other.general`, as an actionable defect.

## Evidence
`billing.premium_paywall` ranks first, with 49,834 complaints [C001] and severity sum 141,749 [C002]. Billing/support represents 20.79% of complaints [A011]. Its share rose from 3.92% early [T009] to 13.04% late [T012], the clearest growth among the areas considered. Representative reviews: `c917e047-2d4b-41c5-ad41-bc9355b6d6e4` objects to being required to pay; `8ce24dbe-f1fe-45cd-bd15-dc210575e5c6` mentions skip limits.

The second-ranked issue, `other.general`, has 66,259 complaints [C005], but is broad dissatisfaction without a specific defect and is non-actionable as a product target. Its share rose from 2.38% [T027] to 17.73% [T030], reinforcing the need not to mistake volume for a fixable issue.

## Alternatives considered
Playback has higher mean severity, 3.188184 [A017], and 26.54% of its complaints are severity four or higher [A021], but its share fell from 8.11% [T033] to 4.55% [T036]. Its defects, including `playback.playback_stops_or_skips` and `playback.crash_freeze`, merit continued reliability work, but are not the leading next-quarter focus.

Access is severe (mean 3.864256 [A038]) and growing, from 0.99% [T003] to 1.83% [T006], but represents 3.33% of complaints [A039]. `access.login_failure` deserves targeted remediation, not the top portfolio priority. Usability is also growing, from 10.98% [T039] to 12.92% [T042], but its mean severity is 2.506640 [A003].

## Limitations
Evidence is from self-selected public reviews, not a customer population. Cancellation records express intent, not observed churn. Trend windows exclude partial first and last months; review classification may leave unresolved boundaries between policy objections and defects.
